questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place that was a fit with my academic interests. And I really wanted to go somewhere, I had never been before and expierence a completly new culture and country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, both University of Copenhagen and Otage University was easy to communicate with and help with the stuff that i was uncertain about.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university provided a service where you could apply for uniflats (flats that were meant for exchange students), which made the whole living situation very easy. And you could go to them for all sorts of questions, and they kept their office open for long periods in the beginning of the semester. They also organised different information meeting you could go to, for different sorts of information and as a way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Sustainability flats and just regular flats usually with five bedrooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: It was a university housing but it wasn't dorms, you shared a house with about four other exchange students, and had your own bedroom and shared a kitchen and bathroom. Therefore I did my own cooking and meal plans, but there was all the necassary cooking facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A really good way to learn some other exchange students. I really liked the house I lived in, but it could be really cold during winter, since lots of the houses are not the best insolated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The application process was fairly simpel, it was through a website called Evision, which you will recieve login. It was very intuitive once you are in the website, and they will send notifications so you know, what need to do, and if they need any extra information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a link to a page with frequently asked questions, and they had a mail adress you could also send questions to

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as soon as possible, and dont be too nervouse about the pre-requirements for subjects neede to take the class, as long as you have had some similar subjects earlier in your study.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two 100 level classes, which did not require a heavy workload, and was mainly aimed for either first years and other students who hadn't taking classes in that field before. I also had a 200 level class, which definetly was a bigger challenge, but I thought it was a very fitting level, where i was able to learn new stuff and was challenged in a good way.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The duration of my classes were shorter at Otago university, lectures only lasted 50 minutes. All the exams were written in hand at Otago University.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Pacific societies, Rivers and runoff, Geographies of sustainble futures

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the course: Pacific societies as i learned a lot. It felt very authentic since a lot of the lectures were from the pacifics themselves, and therefore could speak about their cultures and expierences.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you want to travel then you either need to rent a car or pay for public transport which is not great

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: groceries were more expensive than expected. Since I live a 2 minute walk from university I luckily didn't have to pay much in transpiration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts, they have so many differents activities. They hosted a day in the beginning of the semester were you could sign up and just learn more about the different clubs at the univeristy.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club, because it is a great way to learn some new people. Make sure you attend the activites provided by uniflatts as this was a god way to learn other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and explore all the great nature New Zealand has to offer

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining clubs is a good way to learn some of the local students, and just be brave and open and talk with people in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't really think there was anything

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked how maori culture was incorporated in normal day life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open, try new things and explore the country

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
